claim_text: Turnitin says it found unauthorized activity in some of its customer-facing systems
summary: In a letter to customers dated Nov 23, 2026, Turnitin's CEO says the company recently identified unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing Turnitin systems.
detail: The letter is posted on Turnitin's own help center. It does not say which systems were involved, what the intruders did, or when it happened. BleepingComputer reported the letter on Nov 24 and calls the incident a cyberattack.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Turnitin's own published letter says someone got into its systems without permission.
notes: Organisation's own statement, Tier 1. BleepingComputer relays the same letter; one independence group for the letter's content.

claim_text: Turnitin has called in outside cybersecurity specialists and told police and regulators
summary: Turnitin says that once it found the activity it started its incident response plan, opened an investigation with outside cybersecurity specialists, and notified law enforcement and cyber regulators.
detail: The letter does not name the specialists, the police force or the regulators, or say in which countries they were notified.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Turnitin's own letter describes the steps it took.
notes: Organisation's statement about its own actions, Tier 1.

claim_text: Turnitin is still investigating and watching for more unauthorized activity
summary: Turnitin says its investigation into the nature and full scope of the incident continues, and that it and its outside experts are monitoring its customer-facing systems for any additional unauthorized activity.
detail: Turnitin says it will give more information as circumstances warrant. BleepingComputer says a company representative had no more details to share when it asked.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Turnitin's own letter says the investigation and monitoring continue.
notes: Tier 1. Revisit on any follow-up letter.

claim_text: Whether students' or teachers' data was accessed or taken
summary: Turnitin has not said whether any user data, such as students' names, emails or submitted papers, was accessed or taken.
detail: BleepingComputer notes the company has not disclosed whether user data was accessed or stolen. We found no school or university notice telling students their data was involved.
label: Not established
notes: Key reader question. Settle only with a Turnitin statement, a school notice or a regulator filing.

claim_text: Turnitin says the affected systems do not hold government ID or institutional financial information
summary: Turnitin says the customer-facing systems involved do not collect government identification credentials or institutional financial information.
detail: This limits what could have been in those systems, but the letter does not say what they do hold. It does not mention students' personal details or papers either way.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Turnitin says it; nobody else has checked it.
notes: Organisation's word alone about the scope, so Reported (same rule as the Next page).

claim_text: How the intruders got in, and which systems they reached
summary: Turnitin has not said how the unauthorized activity started or which customer-facing systems were involved.
detail: No source names a flaw, a stolen password or a supplier.
label: Not established
notes: Root cause not published, so the page stays open.

summary: No one has claimed the attack, and Turnitin has not said who was behind it.
detail: BleepingComputer says that as of its report no ransomware group had publicly taken responsibility. We did not check leak sites and will not.
label: Not established
notes: Attribution: none. Do not add claims from leak sites or trackers.

claim_text: When it happened and how many people are affected
summary: Turnitin says only that it 'recently' found the activity. It has not said when the intrusion happened or how many schools, students or teachers might be affected.
detail: Turnitin says its products are used by more than 16,000 institutions in 185 countries and 71 million students, per BleepingComputer, but that is its total reach, not a count of people affected.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source gives a date for the intrusion or a count of people affected.
notes: Do not use the 71 million figure as a victim count.

claim_text: Turnitin says its systems are fully working and safe to use
summary: Turnitin says its systems are fully operational and safe to use. Its status page showed all systems operational on Nov 24, 2026, with no incident logged for November.
detail: BleepingComputer also found no incident or disruption on the status page. 'Safe to use' is Turnitin's own judgement while its investigation is still going on; BleepingComputer notes it is unclear whether uploading sensitive data is safe yet.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Turnitin's letter and its own status page say the service works; only Turnitin says it is safe.
notes: Organisation's word alone on safety, so Reported. Nothing went down, so no service field.
